To summarize, the key findings of our research, stated in one sentence that includes all relevant information, are that
we present the design of a new task oriented, energy aware and heterogeneous container orchestrator.
Heats, a novel task oriented and energy-aware orchestrator, allows customers to trade off performance vs energy consumption in the deployment of containerized applications on heterogeneous clusters.
Heats is the first system that enables energy-aware task-based scheduling of heterogeneous containers.
In summary, our research is concerned with

the following aspects: (i) the design of an orchestrator for containers targeting heterogeneous clusters; (ii) the development of a prototype of such an orchestrator; (iii) the evaluation of the performance and energy benefits of our approach.
the following aspects: 1) We introduce Heats: an energy and performance aware container orchestrator for heterogeneous clusters.

the following aspects of containerized workloads on clusters featuring hardware heterogeneity: 1) how to exploit the hardware diversity offered by cloud providers, 2) how to take into account the energy requirements of different hardware configurations.

our approach is a step in the right direction and that it is a good starting point to further improve the state of the art in this domain.

A comprehensive summary for our work would be that
we introduce the first task oriented and energy efficient orchestrator for container-based applications targeting heterogeneous clusters, and we implement it within Google's Kubernetes.
Heats allows customers and cloud providers to exploit hardware diversity and to trade performance vs energy requirements in their deployments.
we introduce a new approach to exploit hardware heterogeneity and to trade energy vs performance in a containerized cluster.
The main takeaway from our work is that
the performance and energy requirements of tasks should be considered when scheduling them on heterogeneous cluster.
orchestrators should be aware of the energy requirements of tasks, and that customers should be given a way to specify their trade-offs.
container orchestrators need to be designed to take into account the heterogeneity in the hardware features of physical machines and in the energy requirements of the tasks to be executed.
